headline: Approved five-year lease purchase of a special education transportation van, plus 19 teacher and administrator nominations.
summary: Staff hires, resignations, and transfers were reported, and two part-time nutrition helpers were approved for Canal School. A report covered the cell phone ban and a new METRO bus pass program at Westbrook High School. Finance reports noted the annual audit has begun and raised concerns about high electrical costs at Saccarappa School.
decisions: Approved minutes of June 10, 2026 and July 30, 2026, 6-0.
Recommended a joint Facilities / Finance Committee meeting, with Siemens attending, to review high electrical costs at Saccarappa School.
Approved hiring two part-time school nutrition helpers at Canal School, 6-0.
Approved a five-year lease purchase agreement for a special education transportation van using Department of Education PreK funds, 6-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Ms. Cavallaro moved and Ms. Brunette seconded the motion to approve the minutes of June 10, 2026 and Joy 30, 2026 as presented ... Vote: 6 in favor - 0 opposed

Ms. Cavallaro moved and Vice-Chair Katy Rice seconded the motion to approve 12.1.1 CTE Exploratory Teacher / WRVC; ... as presented with 12.1.12 corrected to "replacing Adam Potvin" ... Vote: 7 in favor - 0 opposed
There were concerns raised regarding the high electrical costs at Saccarappa School and a joint Facilities / Finance Committee was recommended with Siemens in attendance to look at those costs.
Vice-Chair Katy Rice moved and Mrs. Poitras seconded the motion to approve hiring two part time school Nutrition Helpers at Canal School for first and final approval ... Vote: 6 in favor - 0 opposed

Vice-Chair Katy Rice moved and Mrs. Poitras seconded the motion to approve a five-year lease purchase agreement for a Special Education Transportation Van with Department of Education PreK funds for first and final approval ... Vote: 6 in favor - 0 opposed

Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia asked Westbrook High School Principal Jeffrey Guerette to report on the cell phone ban at Westbrook High School and the new Metro Bus Pass Program.

Principal Jeffrey Guerette hoped that people would recognize the upgrades and improvements to the high school campus which includes a new scoreboard on Olmsted Field donated by Art Girard, brand new windows on the first floor, new trees in the bus loop. Solar panels that are being dubbed Ragan's Rays to honor former science teacher Ragan Hedstrom who was one of the leading voices to bring solar to Westbrook High School.

Westbrook High School Principal Jeffrey Guerette reported on the new bell-to-bell cell phone ban and the use of Yondr bags for students to use to store their personal devices. There will be a technology forum in Room 114 at Westbrook High School on Tuesday at 6 p.m. to explain the new personal electronic device policy and answer questions from families and students.

Westbrook High School Principal Jeffrey Guerette also announced the start of the student METRO program that was funded by City Council to provide rides to students to help to increase attendance and give students access to jobs, medical appointments and to get to know their surrounding communities.
